title: Dedicated Residency Attestations for Tenant Isolation and Automated Evidence Bundles
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Provide a production-ready implementation to generate signed tenant-level attestations proving data residency and tenant isolation for Dedicated capacity customers. The feature creates an evidence bundle (periodic and on-demand) that includes region placement proofs, node assignment logs, VPC peering and subnet mappings, KMS key bindings, and network isolation test results. Attestations must be cryptographically signed and discoverable by customer compliance teams and Redwood auditors.
acceptance_criteria: For any Dedicated capacity reservation, system can publish a tenant attestation proving all active serving nodes are in the requested region(s) and under the customer's Dedicated pool.

Evidence bundle contains: timestamped node assignment logs (hashes), KMS key fingerprint, VPC/subnet mapping, routing table snapshot or flow logs summary, and results of a tenant-level network isolation test.
Attestations are signed with the platform signing key and exposed via a read-only API endpoint and stored in immutable archive (30/90/365 day retention options configurable per tenant).
Automated monthly evidence export scheduled per tenant with an option for on-demand generation triggered by support or the customer via console or API.
Performance impact of attestation generation on serving latency is negligible (<1% p50 token latency increase) and generation occurs asynchronously when possible.
Security review completed and documented; RBAC enforced for who can request/see attestations.
UI in Console: tenant compliance tab shows latest attestation metadata + link to download evidence bundle and verify signature.
Audit log entries for every attestation generation and download are exported to customer-configurable S3 destinations or syslog endpoints.
implementation_notes: Design a minimal on-path dataplane hook to record node allocation events (node_id, region, pool_id, timestamp) to an append-only ledger (Postgres w/ write-ahead hash chain or S3 object chain) to enable verifiable historical proof.
Leverage existing KMS integration to include key fingerprints in attestation; use key-signing instead of raw private key storage.

Create a signed attestation JSON document schema v1: {tenant_id, reservation_id, period_start, period_end, node_hashes[], ksm_fingerprint, signature, metadata}, and publish both JSON and a verifiable compact digest.
Batch evidence bundle generation as a background job tied to cycle windows to avoid peak serving times; allow immediate on-demand runs which mark a generation flag and queue high-priority job.
Add endpoints: GET /tenants/{id}/attestations (list), GET /tenants/{id}/attestations/{attestation_id} (download bundle + signature).
Retention settings configurable per tenant via console and API: default 90 days; add options 30/90/365 and 'customer-managed S3' for enterprise plans.
Implement tenant isolation tests: ephemeral probe pods that attempt intra-cluster cross-tenant connections and record netcat/tcpdump results; only probe within Dedicated pools with customer consent.
Instrument metrics (attestations_generated_total, generation_latency_seconds, generation_failures) and add alerting if generation fails 3 consecutive times for a tenant.
Prepare DB migration to add attestation_meta table (tenant_id, attestation_id, created_at, storage_path, signature_fingerprint, retention_until, generated_by).
Add a lightweight verification CLI (open-source) customers can run locally to validate signature and digest against the public signing key.
Work with Legal/Privacy to ensure evidence bundles do not leak customer PII; scrub or hash any logs that could contain tokens or user-level data.
compliance_flow: Customer requests Dedicated capacity and selects data residency region(s) and retention policy during provisioning.
Provisioner pins tenant to Dedicated GPU pool nodes in selected regions and records initial assignment ledger entry.
Daily background job consolidates node assignment logs and KV-cache mappings into candidate evidence objects and computes SHA256 hashes.
Monthly or on-demand evidence bundle composed, signed by platform KMS key, and archived with retention policy metadata.
System emits event to customer console and optional webhook/enterprise S3; audit log entry generated for traceability.
Customer or Redwood auditor runs verification tool to confirm signature and cross-check node hashes with published node inventory.
risk_tradeoffs: Cost: storing immutable evidence bundles increases storage costs for long retention (365 days); consider enterprise surcharge or customer-managed S3 for cost isolation.
Latency/Throughput: synchronous generation would impact the serving path; we must keep generation asynchronous with rate limiting to avoid throttling control plane writes.
Complexity: adding ledger and signed bundles increases operational complexity and on-call surface; require runbook updates and recovery playbooks.
Data privacy: logs used for proofs may contain sensitive metadata; must implement deterministic hashing/scrubbing to reduce leakage risk while preserving verifiability.
Legal/Compliance: attestation semantics (what we can legally assert) must be reviewed and limited — avoid absolute language like 'no cross-tenant leakage' without ongoing validation evidence.

Observed negligible CPU overhead on scheduler but ~30ms additional tail latency when writing synchronous metadata; moving to async write reduces to 2ms.
